Genes: ENSG00000117632

{"ENSG00000117632":{"symbol":"STMN1","name":"stathmin 1","summary":"This gene belongs to the stathmin family of genes. It encodes a ubiquitous cytosolic phosphoprotein proposed to function as an intracellular relay integrating regulatory signals of the cellular environment. The encoded protein is involved in the regulation of the microtubule filament system by destabilizing microtubules. It prevents assembly and promotes disassembly of microtubules. Multiple trans"}}

STMN1 is a proliferation marker (regulates microtubule dynamics), classically upregulated in rapidly dividing cells such as proliferating lymphocytes, activated T/B cells, hematopoietic progenitors, and plasmablasts. In PBMC scRNA-seq datasets, a cluster with STMN1 as a top marker is typically identified as a proliferating (cycling) lymphocyte population.

```json
{"cell_type": "Proliferating (cycling) lymphocytes", "confidence": 0.55}
```
